newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn drops to new contract lows on estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn drops to new contract lows on estimate.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower and new contract lows were set in all but the December contracts, traders said.
But nearby December dropped to a fresh 14-month low on bearish input from a private crop estimate, traders said.
"People on the floor were looking for a 9.2, so FCC was a little bearish," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Iowa-based analytical firm Farmers Commodities Corp Monday said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 9.33 billion bushels, above trader expectations for 9.2 billion and above USDA's forecast in October for 9.012 billion.
USDA on November 12 will release its next crop estimate and there are several more private estimates expected out this week.
The new harvest low which also is the fresh 14 month low for December is $2.57-3/4 per bushel. That's the lowest price seen for that contract since $2.57-1/4 was set on August 11, 1995.
The new contract low for March is $2.62-3/4, down from the previous low of $2.67-1/4 set Monday.
Corn closed 3-1/4 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/4 at $2.58-1/2.
Traders also said the market remains technically weak with the key moving averages tilting downward.

December broke below first support at $2.60 and closed between that level and second support which was seen at $2.55-1/2. December closed very oversold for the short term with the daily nine day relative strength (RSI) index ending at 11 points. The market views an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold scenario.

FIMAT vice president Paul Haugens tied the break in corn futures to commercial selling and scant demand. "Commercials were pretty good sellers today and nobody sees any reason right now to pay up," he said.
Cargill Inc sold 4.5 million bushels of March and Tenco Inc sold six million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 69,000 contracts, down from 79,600 Monday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Term Commodities sold 1,000 December $2.60 puts at five cents and Smith Barney bought 500 December 1997 $2.80 puts at 25-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 22,130 Monday.
